title: Git ref and artifact object enumeration capabilities
description:
Objective: add the two ABSENT enumeration capabilities that the recovery-window inventory adapters must call, to the shipped observers/stores that already own those boundaries. This is a prerequisite production task created because the capability is missing, NOT a narrowed DoD and NOT a test-owned reimplementation.

MEASURED GAP at 2026-08-09 by architect-d46fcb95, symbol by symbol:
- `GitObserver` (packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts) declares exactly headCommit(), statusPorcelainV2(), lsFilesTracked(), lsFilesIgnored(), submodulePaths(). There is NO branch or ref enumeration. `grep -rn "for-each-ref|show-ref|--branches|refs/heads|listRefs" packages/runner/src --include=*.ts` (non-test) returns ZERO.
- `ArtifactStore` (packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-contract.ts) declares exactly stageArtifact(), verifyArtifact(), deleteArtifact(); `ArtifactFsPort` declares openWrite/write/fsync/close/exists/rename/persistAfterRename/readAll/unlink. There is NO directory listing. `grep -rn "readdir|listObjects|listStaging|scandir" packages/runner/src` returns ZERO outside runtime-entrypoint.test.ts.

Consequently task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a's DoD 2 ("Git branches/refs ... artifact objects/staging") currently has nothing to call.

Deliverable, additive only:
1. Extend GitObserver with a bounded ref enumeration (refs with their target commit, covering refs/heads and refs/remotes) implemented in createNodeGitObserver via the existing hermetic runGit helper — same shell:false / bounded maxBuffer / timeout / windowsHide discipline, NUL-framed output, and the existing ScopeObserverError codes for overflow and malformed output. Do not loosen hermeticGitEnvironment.
2. Extend ArtifactFsPort with a bounded directory listing and ArtifactStore with object/staging enumeration over the store's own `<root>/objects/<sha256>` layout, implemented in createNodeArtifactFs / createArtifactStore. An entry whose name is not a valid content address is reported as such, never skipped silently.

Both additions are ENUMERATION ONLY: no new mutation, no new authority, no change to any existing method's behaviour or refusal codes.

NOT in scope: the recovery-inventory contract, coverage protocol, or any inventory adapter (those are task-0325dcf7's children); scheduler rows; deciding adopt/quarantine.

Owned paths: packages/runner/src/scope/scope-contract.ts, packages/runner/src/scope/scope-git.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-contract.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-node-fs.ts, packages/runner/src/artifacts/artifact-store.ts, their focused tests, and the minimal @moe/runner root export wiring.

WARNING measured by the architect: packages/runner/src/index-surface.test.ts pins the EXACT root namespace against a hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS list plus a hard-coded `expect(EXPECTED_EXPORTS.length).toBe(116)`. Any new root value export reddens it until transcribed and the count bumped. That file was ALREADY red at 2026-08-09 from an unrelated in-flight task's exports; capture the baseline before editing and attribute per the project's path-attributed-baseline rail.

Consumer (global rail Clause 1): task-0325dcf7ee744123b40cf583230c7b6a's Git/integration and artifact/staging adapter child.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test
definitionOfDone: GitObserver declares a bounded ref enumeration and createNodeGitObserver implements it through the existing hermetic runGit helper with shell:false, bounded maxBuffer, explicit timeout and windowsHide, returning each ref with its target commit; hermeticGitEnvironment is unchanged.

ArtifactFsPort declares a bounded directory listing and ArtifactStore exposes object/staging enumeration over its own <root>/objects/<sha256> layout; an entry whose name is not a valid content address is reported with a stable code, never silently skipped.

Overflow, a malformed or truncated git response, an absent directory, and an unreadable entry each refuse with an existing stable code and the layer that refused; a test pins the exact code and layer for every one, and no failure escapes as an uncoded throw.
Enumeration output is deterministic across path separators and locale on Windows, macOS and Linux; ordering is canonical and a generated sweep asserts a non-zero case count.
No existing method's behaviour, signature, or refusal code changes; the pre-existing scope and artifact suites still pass unmodified except where a new capability is added to a frozen list.

New root value exports are transcribed into index-surface.test.ts's hand-written EXPECTED_EXPORTS with the count literal bumped, and fresh pnpm --filter @moe/runner typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/runner test exits 0 with any residual red attributed to foreign paths against a recorded merge-base baseline.
taskRails: Additive enumeration only. Do not change, relax, or re-code any existing observer/store method or refusal code; a behaviour change here silently alters every scope observation and artifact receipt already in production.
These are external-effect boundaries: never invoke git through a shell, never accept a free-form command string, and keep every child bounded by maxBuffer, timeout and windowsHide.
A missing directory, an empty listing, and an unreadable entry are three different facts and must carry three different answers; an empty result is never proof of absence.
Tests assert the exact stable reason code and the refusing layer, and any generated sweep asserts it produced a non-zero number of cases.
Target <=250 physical lines per production file and split before 400; this cap is per file, not per task.

implementationPlan.description: TDD RED: add focused production-surface tests for createNodeGitObserver().listRefs() and createArtifactStore().enumerateArtifacts(). The Git matrix must cover real head/remote refs plus injected invalid UTF-8, truncated NUL fields/LF record termination, wrong field count, out-of-scope/duplicate ref, non-commit target, lowercase 40/64-hex validation, empty observation, generic/timeout failure, and both Node overflow shapes; every refusal asserts exact code and GIT_OBSERVER layer. The artifact matrix must cover real temp-store objects/staging, missing versus successful-empty versus unreadable listing/entry, unavailable optional FS capability, N/N+1 overflow, invalid/duplicate/non-file/symlink names, object-address mismatch, staging grammar, and permutation/path-separator/locale independence; assert exact code and ARTIFACT_FS_PORT or ARTIFACT_STORE layer. Hand-author case tables, assert each table length is >0, and assert exact generated/executed ID-set equality so a zero/filtered sweep cannot pass.
implementationPlan.note:
TDD RED established. 37 new tests, 30 failing, and every failure is a missing symbol rather than a wrong assertion — `store.enumerateArtifacts is not a function`, `listRefs is not implemented`, `parseRefListing` unresolved. That is the correct RED shape: the tests describe a surface that does not exist yet, not one that exists and misbehaves.

WHY THE GIT SIDE IS COVERED FROM TWO DIRECTIONS. Real git is spawned against a temp repository built per test (init, one commit on main, a second branch, plus `update-ref refs/remotes/origin/main` so refs/remotes is genuinely populated without a network). A fake observer would prove only that the fake agrees with itself — argv, the hermetic environment and git's actual for-each-ref grammar are precisely what a fake cannot check. The malformed cases then drive `parseRefListing` directly, because real git cannot be made to emit invalid UTF-8 or a truncated record on demand; those branches are unreachable any other way. That parser is production code that `listRefs()` itself calls, NOT a test reimplementation — epic rail 6's distinction.

CASE TABLES ARE GUARDED, NOT JUST WRITTEN. Both suites assert `length > 0`, an exact literal count (10 git malformed cases, 8 artifact refusals) and that the id set is duplicate-free. A sweep that silently produced zero cases would otherwise pass while testing nothing.

EVERY REFUSAL PINS CODE **AND** LAYER. Git: invalid UTF-8, record not LF-terminated, truncated field count, extra field, empty ref name, out-of-scope ref, duplicate ref, non-commit target, uppercase hex, short hex — all RUNNER_SCOPE_STATUS_MALFORMED + GIT_OBSERVER. Missing repository -> RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_FAILED + GIT_OBSERVER. Artifacts: absent objects dir -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_MISSING/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; unreadable listing -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; port without the optional capability -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE/ARTIFACT_STORE; N+1 -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LIMIT/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; unrecognised name, uppercase address, bytes-not-matching-address, directory-in-place-of-object -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT/ARTIFACT_STORE. Asserting the layer is what stops a second refusal layer starting to answer first while the test stays green.

THE THREE-FACT RAIL IS ASSERTED AS THREE ANSWERS. Missing directory (refusal), successful empty listing (ok, empty, WITH a digest), and unreadable entry (different code) are separate cases. A successful empty observation still carries `observationDigest`, so a caller can tell "looked, nothing there" from "could not look" — an empty array for a missing directory is exactly the collapse the rail forbids.

DETERMINISM IS ASSERTED AGAINST AN ADVERSARIAL PORT, not just observed. The ordering test injects a port whose `listDirectory` returns entries REVERSED and requires the identical entry order and the identical observationDigest. Sorting that only ever sees pre-sorted input is untested sorting. Code-unit vs locale is pinned separately with refs A/a/b, where locale collation would give a different answer than the required one.

ONE HONEST GAP, DECLARED. The symlink case cannot run unprivileged on Windows. Rather than skip it silently — which would make it vacuous exactly like a zero-case sweep — the catch branch asserts `process.platform === "win32"`, so on a POSIX host the case must really execute and on this host the reason for not executing is itself pinned.

CONTRACT SHAPE THIS RED IMPLIES, for step 3: ScopeObserverError gains an OPTIONAL third constructor argument carrying the layer, so all existing two-argument throws keep byte-identical behaviour and only the listRefs path tags GIT_OBSERVER. `ArtifactFsPort.listDirectory` is optional so existing injected ports stay source-compatible; the store fails closed with ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE when it is absent. No existing method signature or code changes.

Baseline unchanged and still green outside the new files: the 41 pre-existing suites are untouched.

THREE COMPATIBILITY DECISIONS, each made to avoid a change the rails forbid:

1. `ScopeObserverError.layer` is OPTIONAL and the THIRD constructor argument. Every existing two-argument throw keeps its exact code and message and now simply reports `layer === undefined`. Making it required would have forced edits at five observer methods this task must not touch.

2. `ArtifactFsPort.listDirectory` is OPTIONAL, `ArtifactStore.enumerateArtifacts` is REQUIRED. The asymmetry is deliberate: the PORT is injected by existing callers and tests, so a required method would break them at compile time; the STORE is factory-owned, so nothing outside this package constructs one. A port without the capability fails closed with ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE rather than reporting an empty directory it never read.

implementationPlan.description: Implement Git ref enumeration in scope-git.ts through the existing runGit boundary only: fixed argv for `for-each-ref --sort=refname --format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(objecttype)%00 refs/heads refs/remotes`, inherited hermetic environment unchanged, shell:false, bounded maxBuffer, explicit timeout, windowsHide, and no free-form command input. Parse Git's exact NUL-delimited fields plus mandatory LF record terminators with fatal UTF-8; require refs/heads or refs/remotes, objecttype=commit, unique canonical ref names, and lowercase 40/64-hex commit identities; code-unit sort, freeze, and digest the canonical observation. Preserve existing runGit callers' refusal mapping byte-for-byte by making ENOBUFS-as-overflow classification operation-scoped to listRefs; malformed/truncated output is RUNNER_SCOPE_STATUS_MALFORMED/GIT_OBSERVER, bounded overflow is RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW/GIT_OBSERVER, and other spawn/nonzero/timeout faults are RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_FAILED/GIT_OBSERVER.
implementationPlan.note:
GIT REF ENUMERATION IMPLEMENTED AND GREEN. All 21 scope-git tests pass; full runner suite 43 files / 1366 tests, exit 0; typecheck exit 0.

ARGV IS FIXED, NOT COMPOSED: `for-each-ref --sort=refname --format=%(refname)%00%(objectname)%00%(objecttype)%00 refs/heads refs/remotes`, routed through the EXISTING runGit helper, so it inherits shell:false, maxBuffer 8 MiB, the 30 s timeout, windowsHide, stdio ignore/pipe/ignore and the unchanged hermeticGitEnvironment. No free-form command string exists anywhere on this path. A test asserts hermeticGitEnvironment still strips GIT_DIR and still pins GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM / GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS / LC_ALL.

THE LF IS PART OF THE GRAMMAR, NOT NOISE. `for-each-ref` has no `-z` mode, so the safe shape is NUL between fields with one LF terminating each record. The parser VALIDATES that terminator rather than trimming it: permissive trimming is exactly how a truncated final record becomes an invisible short listing. Required per record: exactly three NUL-framed fields plus the trailing NUL (a 4-way split whose last element is empty), a name under refs/heads or refs/remotes, objecttype `commit`, and a LOWERCASE 40- or 64-hex target. Duplicates refuse. Out-of-scope refs refuse rather than being dropped — a parser that silently skips what it does not recognise cannot tell a scope change from a bug.

OPERATION-SCOPED CLASSIFICATION, so no existing caller shifts. listRefs wraps only its own spawn. Real win32 execFileSync can report an overflow as ENOBUFS, which runGit maps to RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_FAILED; widening runGit itself would have re-classified failures for the other five methods. Instead runGit now attaches the original error as `cause` — PURELY ADDITIVE, code and message byte-identical, verified by the five untouched observer suites — and listRefs' wrapper reads that cause to promote ENOBUFS to RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW and to tag GIT_OBSERVER. Malformed -> RUNNER_SCOPE_STATUS_MALFORMED/GIT_OBSERVER, overflow -> RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_OVERFLOW/GIT_OBSERVER, everything else -> RUNNER_SCOPE_OBSERVATION_FAILED/GIT_OBSERVER.

FILE SPLIT, AND WHY IT WAS NOT OPTIONAL. Implementing in place put scope-git.ts at 326 physical lines — 30% over the 250 target. The parser moved to a new scope-refs.ts (101 lines) with its required one-line LF `.js` bridge, taking scope-git.ts to exactly 250. This is the split the rails prescribe ("per-file violations are fixed by splitting the file") and the responsibilities really are different: one is an external process effect, the other a pure function. scope-git.ts re-exports parseRefListing, so the name stays reachable exactly where it was and no test import had to change.

DEVIATION FROM PLAN SHAPE, DECLARED. The plan named 9 affected files; I am at 13 (added artifact-enumeration.ts/.js and scope-refs.ts/.js, each a module plus its mandatory bridge). Both additions exist solely to keep a production file under the cap — artifact-store.ts had ~40 lines of headroom and the enumerator needs ~165. The alternative was two files over target, which the rails treat as the real violation. Not asking forgiveness for hidden scope: no new behaviour came with these files, only relocation.

BRIDGES: scope-refs.js and artifact-enumeration.js both created as exact LF one-liners and verified with `od -c`. Omitting them fails NOTHING in tsc or vitest and only breaks the plain-Node runtime entrypoint — the known trap recorded in Serena as gotcha-scheduler-js-shims / gotcha-vitest-hides-missing-js-bridge.

ONE TEST DEFECT I FOUND IN MY OWN TEST AND FIXED BEFORE IT LIED. The digest-separation case builds two temp repositories and asserts their observation digests differ. With GIT_AUTHOR_DATE/GIT_COMMITTER_DATE pinned to @0 and identical content, author and message, git produces the IDENTICAL commit id — so the assertion would have failed, and the obvious "fix" of unpinning the dates would have made it pass for the wrong reason (nondeterminism, not content sensitivity). The seed file content is now unique per repository instead, so the digest is separated by content while the build stays reproducible.

implementationPlan.description: Implement bounded artifact enumeration without changing stage/verify/delete behavior. createNodeArtifactFs.listDirectory must incrementally use Node directory handles, stop and close at N+1, return basename plus FILE|DIRECTORY|OTHER only, distinguish a missing objects directory from unreadable open/read/close, and expose no raw path/error. createArtifactStore.enumerateArtifacts performs one scan of `<root>/objects`, code-unit sorts a copy, recognizes only lowercase 64-hex object addresses or the exact existing `<16hex>.<safe-counter>.tmp` staging grammar, reads every file through the production port, verifies object bytes hash to their address, hashes/sizes staging bytes, rejects duplicate/raced/non-file/symlink/unrecognized entries rather than skipping, and returns frozen entries plus canonical observation digest/count. Pin missing as RUNNER_ARTIFACT_MISSING/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT, unreadable as RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT, N+1 as RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LIMIT/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT, missing optional listing as RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE/ARTIFACT_STORE, and invalid content/layout as RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT/ARTIFACT_STORE.
implementationPlan.note:
ARTIFACT ENUMERATION IMPLEMENTED AND GREEN. All 16 enumeration tests pass; full runner suite 43 files / 1366 tests, exit 0; typecheck exit 0. artifact-store.ts's own pre-existing suite is untouched and still passes.

PORT SIDE — createNodeArtifactFs.listDirectory. Uses `opendirSync` + incremental `readSync`, NOT readdirSync. That is the whole point: readdirSync materialises the entire listing before any ceiling can reject it, so a directory with millions of entries would be fully allocated before the bound applied. The handle stops at MAX+1 and `finally { handle.closeSync() }` closes it on the normal, overflow and error paths alike — an unclosed directory handle on win32 keeps the directory locked against later renames, which would silently break staging. Only a BASENAME and a coarse FILE|DIRECTORY|OTHER kind escape; no raw path and no OS error text. Symlinks report OTHER rather than being followed, so the store refuses them explicitly instead of reading through them.

STORE SIDE — enumerateArtifacts. One scan of `<root>/objects`. Entries are code-unit sorted BEFORE anything is read, so a port listing in a different order produces byte-identical output. Only two names are recognised: a lowercase 64-hex address, or the store's own existing `<16hex>.<counter>.tmp` staging grammar. Object bytes are re-hashed and must equal their own filename — an enumerator that reported the name without checking it would launder corruption into an inventory. Anything else is REPORTED, never skipped.

CODE/LAYER PAIRS, all pinned by test: missing objects dir -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_MISSING/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; unreadable listing or entry -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_VERIFY_FAILED/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; N+1 -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_LIMIT/ARTIFACT_FS_PORT; port lacking the optional capability -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ENUMERATION_UNAVAILABLE/ARTIFACT_STORE; unrecognised name, uppercase address, bytes-not-matching-address, directory or symlink in an object slot -> RUNNER_ARTIFACT_ADDRESS_CORRUPT/ARTIFACT_STORE. The FS_PORT/STORE division is not decorative: it separates "the filesystem could not tell me" from "what it told me is not a valid layout", and a test asserts the layer so a future refactor cannot let the wrong boundary start answering while the codes still look right.

THE THREE-FACT RAIL IS HONOURED IN THE RETURN TYPE, NOT JUST THE TESTS. Missing refuses; readable-but-empty SUCCEEDS carrying entryCount 0 and a real observationDigest; unreadable refuses with a different code. There is no code path that returns an empty array for a directory it failed to read.

NEW FILE, DECLARED. The enumerator is 165 lines and artifact-store.ts had roughly 40 lines of headroom under the cap, so it lives in artifact-enumeration.ts with its required LF `.js` bridge; the store delegates in three lines and ends at 211. The plan's own risk note called this out in advance ("keep the enumeration delegate focused; ... rather than compressing past 400 or adding a helper without its required bridge") — the bridge is present and `od -c` verified.

NO RAW PATH LEAKS, ASSERTED NOT ASSUMED. Every refusal case asserts `result.message` does not contain the temp root. The catch around listDirectory deliberately drops the OS error text because it carries absolute paths.

NOTHING EXISTING CHANGED. stageArtifact, verifyArtifact and deleteArtifact are byte-identical; a test drives all three end to end and asserts the exact same results as before. ArtifactFsPort gained only an optional method, so every port already injected elsewhere still compiles.

ONE HONEST LIMIT ON THE SYMLINK CASE. It cannot run unprivileged on Windows, which is this host. Rather than skip it silently — vacuous in exactly the way epic rail 6 names — the catch branch asserts `process.platform === "win32"`, so on a POSIX host the case must really execute, and here the reason it did not is itself pinned. On this run that case proved the platform, not the behaviour, and I am not claiming otherwise.
